result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Select all nodes within K hops of specified seed nodes. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Select all nodes within K hops of specified seed nodes. title: >- [Graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Select all nodes within K hops of specified seed nodes. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select all nodes within K hops of specified seed nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23743-L23880){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood( nodes, k=1, mode="out", set_op="union", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Select nodes in neighborhood](/assets/graphs/select-nodes-in-neighborhood.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node grid with no selection. After select_nodes_in_neighborhood from seed A with k=2, badges give each node's hop distance from A, and every node within two hops is selected in the accent color: A itself, B and D at one hop, and C and E at two. F, three hops away, is not selected." width="100%"} Runs a breadth-first search from the seed nodes and selects every node at distance at most `k`. The seed nodes themselves (distance 0) are always included. With several seeds, the result is the union of their neighborhoods. K-hop neighborhoods (often called ego networks) are useful for: - extracting the local context around a node of interest, e.g., with `transform_to_subgraph_ws()` afterwards - finding everything upstream (`mode="in"`) or downstream (`mode="out"`) of a node within a limited number of steps, such as the blast radius of a failing service - restricting expensive analyses to a manageable region of a large graph Distances count edges, not weights. In a directed graph, `mode=` decides which edges can be followed; in an undirected graph every edge can be followed regardless of `mode=`. The neighborhood grows quickly with `k` in well-connected graphs (the whole graph is often reached within a handful of hops). The neighborhood is added to the current selection, unless `set_op=` says otherwise. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | int | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Seed node(s) to start from. Can be a single node ID (int), a single label (str), or a list mixing IDs and labels. An unknown label or node ID raises `ValueError`. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of hops from the seeds. Defaults to `1` (seeds plus their direct neighbors). `k=0` selects only the seeds. Must be a non-negative integer. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which edges to follow in a directed graph: `"out"` (default) follows edges from source to target (successors, downstream), `"in"` follows them backwards (predecessors, upstream), and `"all"` ignores direction. Any other value raises `ValueError`. For undirected graphs the value is still validated but the traversal always behaves like `"all"`. [set_op]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["union"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How the selected nodes combine with the current node selection. `"union"` (default) adds them to it, `"replace"` makes them the selection, `"intersect"` keeps only the selected nodes among them, and `"difference"` removes them from it. Any edge selection is cleared, since the graph holds a selection of nodes or of edges but not both. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `mode=` is not one of `"out"`, `"in"`, or `"all"`, if a seed node does not exist, or if `set_op=` is not `"union"`, `"replace"`, `"intersect"`, or `"difference"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a 5-node star, a 1-hop selection from the hub reaches every spoke; together with the hub itself that is all 5 nodes. The hub is the first node the generator creates: ::: {#0e855eb5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(n=5) center_id = graph.get_node_creation_order()[0] graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood(nodes=center_id, k=1, mode="all") graph.count_selected_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 5 ``` ::: ::: Increasing `k` extends the reach further along the graph. Starting from "A" with `k=2` and following outgoing edges selects "A" plus "B" and "C", but not "D", which is three hops away: ::: {#06dcfdfb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ) graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood(nodes="A", k=2, mode="out") sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C'] ``` ::: ::: Direction matters in directed graphs. In the same graph, following edges backwards from "C" with `mode="in"` finds its upstream nodes instead -- "C", "B", and "A" -- and never reaches "D": ::: {#f5b58294 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood(nodes="C", k=2, mode="in") sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C'] ``` ::: ::: Multiple seed nodes are unioned together -- here, the 1-hop neighborhoods of both "A" and "B" combine with the seeds themselves, leaving out only "E" (two hops from "A" via "C"): ::: {#5cb3d981 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "E")]) ) graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood(nodes=["A", "B"], k=1, mode="all") sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'] ``` ::: :::
